idiom_name: @ID(key: .id) property wrapper with Fluent (or Core Data NSManagedObjectID)
implementation_notes: Fluent (Vapor) puts identity into a property wrapper: every Model needs @ID(key: .id) var id: UUID?, the value is nil until the model is saved, requireID() throws for an unsaved instance, and $id.exists tracks whether the row is known to the database. The generation strategy is chosen explicitly with @ID(custom:generatedBy:) - .database lets the store assign an auto-increment column, .random uses a RandomGeneratable type such as UUID, .user expects the application to set the value before saving - which is exactly the classic key-generator decision made declarative. Core Data/SwiftData take the other route and keep identity in NSManagedObjectID/PersistentIdentifier rather than in a stored attribute.
pitfalls: requireID() throws and id is optional by design: force-unwrapping ($id!) before the save is the classic Fluent crash.

generatedBy: .database needs a database-generated column and is unsupported by NoSQL drivers; .random/.user are the portable choices, and a mismatch between the property type and the migration column type surfaces only at runtime.
Mutating $id.exists by hand desynchronises Fluent's view of whether the model is persisted, so subsequent save/update calls take the wrong path.
